Treating it as a plain Position would produce wrong-shaped scoring (a TWP would either bat or pitch in a stat line, not both).
Out of scope for Phase 1 of the engine. When implemented, expect a separate two-way-player concept rather than a Position constructor.

parsePosition: accepts BOTH MLB numeric codes ('1','2',...,'10') AND scorer abbreviations ('P','C','1B','2B','3B','SS','LF','CF','RF','DH')
returns Nothing for 'TWP' (intentional — see decision TwoWayPlayerNotModelled)
renderPosition: returns the scorer form (the more human-readable of the two parse options)
isPitcher: True for Pitcher only; False for everything else including DH
isInfielder: True for FirstBase, SecondBase, ThirdBase, Shortstop, AND Catcher
Catcher being an infielder is conventional for fantasy classification; some literature treats Catcher separately
isOutfielder: True for LeftField, CenterField, RightField; False for everything else
DH is not an outfielder despite the position number 10 being adjacent to the OF positions

decisions.name: ModuleStructureNotes
decisions.what: What this module exports (only parse/render functions have signatures; the Player record is a data declaration)
why: Player record holds: PlayerId, denormalised first/last/slug names, Maybe TeamId, Maybe Position, Maybe Handedness for batting and pitching, and a non-Maybe active flag.
Handedness sum: LeftHanded | RightHanded | Switch. MLB encodes these as 'L', 'R', 'S' and we track this exactly.
playerActive is non-Maybe; absence at the wire layer is a parse error.
Field-level documentation lives in the source comments and is preserved verbatim by chase's data decl rendering.

parseHandedness: consumed by Pelotero.MLB.Convert.convertHand to convert a wire code to Handedness
renderHandedness: consumed by Pelotero.Sync.Players.upsertAllPlayers via T.head to convert to single-character DB representation

decisions.name: ModuleStructureNotes
decisions.what: Module exports only the Team data declaration; no functions
why: Team has: TeamId (upstream MLB id), full name (e.g. 'Houston Astros'), abbreviation ('HOU'), and location name (the city, e.g. 'Houston').
No division/league/venue at this layer — see Pelotero.MLB.Wire.Team decision WireTeamMinimalFields.
No constructor or smart-constructor; tests build with record syntax directly.

decisions.name: ModuleStructureNotes
decisions.what: Module exports only data declarations; no functions
why: Game has: GameId, gameDate (Day, NOT UTCTime — see Pelotero.DB.Game decision GameDateAsDay), away/home team ids.
No game state (scheduled/final) at this layer; that comes from a separate fetch path (Pelotero.MLB.Urls.gameStatusUrl, currently unused).

GameSchedule wraps a flat [Game]; an off-day or all-star break is represented as an empty list, NOT a Maybe. Callers needing to distinguish 'no schedule fetched' from 'no games on this day' must do so at a higher layer.

decisions.name: MaybeIntPerField
decisions.what: Every stat field in the per-game stats records is Maybe Int rather than Int with a default of 0
why: Distinguishes 'didn't bat' from 'batted, went 0-for-0'.
A pitcher's batting line in the AL legitimately has Nothing for atBats, not 0 — a 0 would falsely imply a plate appearance.
Scoring layer applies fromMaybe 0 at the point of multiplication; presence/absence info is preserved up to that point.

decisions.name: InningsPitchedAsTextThenOuts
decisions.what: pitInningsPitched is Maybe Text (the wire string, e.g. '6.2'); parseInningsPitched converts to outs (Int)
why: Storing the wire string preserves the source-of-truth representation through the domain layer.
Conversion to outs is the FIRST thing the scoring layer does; treating 6.2 as a Double silently corrupts data (legacy bug).
Outs (multiples of 1/3 inning) make arithmetic exact; a database column stores them as INTEGER (Pelotero.DB.BoxscoreEntry _pInningsPitchedOuts).

emptyBatting: all-Nothing default for every BattingStats field; useful for parser fallbacks (a player with no batting stats becomes emptyBatting, not a partial record with some Nothings)
BattingStats has 25 Maybe Int fields; all wire-derived; no derived stats at this layer (singles, batting average) — those are computed at scoring time
emptyPitching: PitchingStats has ~40 Maybe Int fields plus pitInningsPitched as Maybe Text and pitOuts as Maybe Int
having both inningsPitched AND outs is redundant by design — the wire ships both, we keep both, and the scoring layer prefers outs derived from parseInningsPitched (more reliable)
parseInningsPitched: the fractional part must be 0, 1, or 2; '6.3' returns Nothing (not a valid IP)
negative whole or fractional parts return Nothing
renderInningsPitched: negative input -> '0.0' (defensive — should never receive negative input)

decisions.name: SeqForOrderedSlotMembers
decisions.what: Roster and Lineup both use Map RosterSlot (Seq PlayerId) — Seq, not List or Set
why: Order matters within a slot (e.g. batting order in a lineup, depth chart in a roster).
Set would lose ordering and require a separate ordering scheme.
List has O(n) appends; Seq has O(log n).
The slot order itself doesn't matter (Map handles that), but the order within a slot does.

decisions.name: ValidationProducesAllErrorsNotJustFirst
decisions.what: validateRoster and validateLineup return [RosterError] / [LineupError] — all problems, not just the first
why: When showing errors in a UI, displaying 'too many at OF (3 vs 2)' AND 'duplicate player X' is more useful than 'too many at OF, retry'.
The cost is a slightly less efficient validator; the ergonomic win is large.
Order is: all size problems then all duplicate problems.

decisions.name: JsonSerialisationViaMap
decisions.what: RosterLimits / LineupLimits ToJSON encodes via Map.mapKeys renderRosterSlot; FromJSON parses with parseRosterSlot
why: JSONB storage in league_config requires round-trippable encodings.
Using the slot's Text representation (renderRosterSlot) keeps the JSON readable to humans (PostgreSQL pgAdmin views, etc.).
Unknown slot keys at parse time fail loudly with the offending key in the message.
Storing as a Text-keyed JSON object rather than an array of [slot, count] pairs aligns with PostgreSQL JSONB indexing patterns.

allRosterSlots: [minBound .. maxBound]; the canonical traversal order is the constructor order in RosterSlot
consumed by emptyRoster, emptyLineup, validateRoster, validateLineup
parseRosterSlot: the s_pitcher / r_pitcher names match legacy DB schema; not 'starter' / 'reliever'
isPitcherSlot: True for SlotStartingPitcher and SlotReliefPitcher; False for everything else
isBatterSlot: = not . isPitcherSlot; SlotUtility is a batter slot
emptyRoster: every slot present with empty Seq; ensures countAt and validation don't have to special-case missing slots
rosterAt: returns Seq.empty if the slot is somehow missing from the map (defensive — shouldn't happen with emptyRoster)
addToRoster: appends to the slot's Seq using the Map.insertWith trick: if slot exists, Seq |> pid; if not, single Seq
no validation against limits at this point — call validateRoster after to detect
removeFromRoster: removes the FIRST occurrence of pid from the slot's Seq; subsequent occurrences (which shouldn't exist after dedup, but might during transitional states) remain
does nothing if the slot or pid is absent
seqRemoveFirst: private; uses Seq.breakl + Seq.viewl to split-and-rejoin
O(log n) for a balanced Seq
rosterPlayers: concatMap toList over slot Seqs; ordering is slot-order (Map.elems) then within-slot order
rosterContains: linear scan via elem; O(total roster size)
countAt: Seq.length on the slot; O(1) since Seq tracks its size
rosterLimitFor: Map lookup; defaults to 0 if the slot has no entry in the limits
validateRoster: produces all over-limit errors then all duplicate errors
duplicates are detected via group . sort, so the resulting list is in PlayerId order, not insertion order
validateLineup: mirror of validateRoster but with LineupError variants
duplicates: private; group . sort then take first of each group of size >= 2

decisions.name: PointsAsRationalNotDouble
decisions.what: The Points newtype wraps Rational, not Double
why: Sums of fantasy points across many games accumulate; floating drift is observable when a season total visibly disagrees with the sum of game lines.
Owners notice this and lose trust in the system.
Cost: marginally slower arithmetic; for the size of fantasy datasets (hundreds of players, ~150 games each), irrelevant.
Scaling by Rational multipliers (e.g. 1/3 for innings) stays exact end-to-end.

decisions.name: MultiplierFieldsAsExplicitRecord
decisions.what: The batting and pitching multiplier records list every scored stat as a named field
why: A Map String Rational would defer typo detection to runtime.
Adding a stat is a structural change on purpose: the compiler tells you about every league config that needs an updated value, every JSON encoder/decoder that needs the new field.
The cost is verbose Aeson instances, accepted because they're write-once.

decisions.name: DerivedStatsInScoringNotData
decisions.what: Singles (batting) and quality starts (pitching) are derived inside scoreBatting / scorePitching, not stored as fields
why: Singles = hits - (doubles + triples + homeRuns); the wire layer doesn't ship singles separately.
Quality start = IP >= 6 AND ER <= 3; not a stat the boxscore reports.
Computing inside the scorer keeps the Stats data type close to what the wire format gives, with derivation as a presentation concern.

decisions.name: InningsPitchedExactRationalArithmetic
decisions.what: scorePitching computes 'pmInningPitched * (outs / 3)' as Rational, not as a Double or pre-rounded decimal
why: Per-inning multipliers are typically integers or simple fractions; fractional outs (e.g. 20 outs = 20/3 innings) need exact division.
Pre-rounding to e.g. 2 decimal places loses ~0.05 points per fractional inning, which compounds over 150 starts.

subPoints: pointwise Rational subtraction; can produce negative Points (e.g. for penalty stats like strikeouts)
currently has no in-tree caller; effectively dead code retained for symmetry with addPoints
scalePoints: multiplies Points by a Rational; preserves exactness
sumPoints: left-fold over a Foldable; uses zeroPoints as the seed
scoreBatting: sums per-stat contributions; each contribution is multiplier * count
singles are derived: max 0 of (hits - doubles - triples - homeRuns) — clamped to zero in case of inconsistent input
missing stats default to 0 via fromMaybe; an empty BattingStats produces zeroPoints
scorePitching: outs come from parseInningsPitched . pitInningsPitched (NOT pitOuts directly — see Pelotero.Domain.Stats decision)
qualityStarts is 1 if outs >= 18 (6 innings) AND earnedRuns <= 3, else 0
innings-pitched contribution uses Rational (outs/3) for exactness

decisions.name: PureOrderGenerator
decisions.what: generateDraftOrder is pure (no IO, no Random); randomness is supplied by the caller as the order of the input team list
why: Pure functions are testable without any randomness effect.
If the caller wants random ordering (a coin flip for first pick), they shuffle the team list outside this module and pass it in.
Keeps this module free of effects; the same ordering algorithm runs identically in production, in tests, and in CLI 'preview' commands.

decisions.name: TruncateTrailingPartialRound
decisions.what: If totalPicks is not a multiple of length teams, the trailing partial round is dropped, NOT half-completed
why: A draft with N teams should always have a multiple-of-N pick count; non-multiples imply a configuration error.
Half-completing a round would create an asymmetry — some teams pick more times than others — which is unfair.
Truncating loudly preserves the 'teams are equal' invariant; the caller can detect the truncation by length-checking the output.

decisions.name: NoActiveDraftStateMachineHere
decisions.what: This module has DraftPick (a record of a made pick) but NO state machine for running a draft
why: A live draft needs database writes per pick (depending on the effects layer).
Putting the state machine here would force this module to depend on the effects layer, which it currently doesn't.
Phase 5 work; designed but not yet implemented.

generateDraftOrder.intent: Produce the full pick-by-pick order as (team, pickNumber)
notes: empty teams returns []; preserves total integrity
rounds = totalPicks `div` length teams; trailing partial round is truncated (see decision)
pick numbers are 1-indexed
pure: no randomness, no IO

serpentine: private; rounds copies of [teams, reverse teams] alternating
round 1 picks in input order; round 2 in reverse; round 3 in input order; etc.
experimentalSnake: private; rounds copies of [teams, mid-shifted, reverse, mid-shifted-reverse] alternating
mid-shift = rotation by half the team count
reproduces the legacy 'experimental_snake' algorithm; matches whatever the prior system did
rankingPlayerIds: extracts just the PlayerIds from a Ranking, in rank order
assumes Ranking.rankingEntries was constructed in rank order — does NOT sort
extendRankingsWithUnranked: appends unranked players (those in universe but not in ranked) to the end of ranked, preserving universe order for the unranked
used by the auto-drafter when a team's ranking is shorter than the player pool

openIssues.name: CremDraftStateMachineNotImplemented
openIssues.what: The original refactor plan called for a crem state machine with WaitingToStart | Drafting | Complete states; the module has DraftPick records but no machine that transitions between states
why: generateDraftOrder is the pure pre-computation; running an actual draft requires per-pick database writes (DraftPick effect), which means the state machine has to live somewhere with effect access — probably a new Pelotero.Draft module, not in Pelotero.Domain.Draft.
This is the load-bearing replacement for the legacy (state, Maybe String) referential-equality detector in old_src/League/Draft.hs.
Until this exists, AutoDraft.hs's behaviour cannot be ported; that executable depends on the state machine to run.
crem is the natural fit (finite states, well-defined transitions, Generic-derivable singletons) and Cheeblr already uses it — same machinery, different domain.

decisions.name: LeagueStatusOnlyMutableField
decisions.what: League's only field that changes after creation is leagueStatus; everything else is the immutable league definition
why: Scoring rules, roster limits, and draft params shouldn't change mid-season; allowing them to would invalidate prior scoring.
Status moves through draft -> active -> closed in the lifecycle.
Per-team rosters and lineups live in FantasyTeam, not in League — keeping League immutable keeps it cacheable.

decisions.name: ScoringPeriodAsUtcTime
decisions.what: ScoringPeriod uses UTCTime, not Day
why: Real leagues have lineup-lock cutoffs at specific game start times in specific timezones.
Day would be ambiguous: does the period end at midnight local? Midnight UTC?
UTCTime forces an explicit instant. The wire layer already gives us instants for game starts.

decisions.name: ModuleStructureNotes
decisions.what: Module exports the data declarations that make a complete league configuration
why: League: top-level config with id, commissioner, status, scoring, roster/lineup limits, draft params, scoring period, and a list of FantasyTeamIds.
FantasyTeam: a single team within a league with id, league reference, name, owner, current Roster, current Lineup.
ScoringPeriod: UTCTime start/end window during which boxscore stats count.
DraftParameters: auto-draft flag, strategy (DraftOrderStrategy), and auto-draft trigger time.
LeagueStatus sum: LeagueDraft | LeagueActive | LeagueClosed.
